description: A modular, stack-agnostic toolkit for AI coding agents to autonomously find, reproduce, and patch vulnerabilities.

written.description: Reads a codebase and its commit history, builds a threat model from them, and sends agents to chase each hypothesis it raises. It then tries to reproduce each finding in a sandbox and attacks its own patch to check the fix holds, working from source alone with no running target.

alive.last_commit_message:
Close the two remaining threat-model leak paths

Follow-up to "Scope single-file scan threat models to their file":
file-scoped concept rows fixed the common case, but two paths still
leaked one file's threat model into another file's security guidance.

- Unscanned files: with every concept row now file-scoped, guidance
  for a file with no rows of its own fell through to the raw
  campaign_artifacts fallback, which served the newest threat model
  artifact regardless of which file its campaign scanned. The fallback
  now checks the stored campaign target: another file's threat model
  is never inherited, while repo-wide rows and the file's own rows
  (e.g. the structured JSON artifact that never produces a concept
  row) still apply, and unparseable metadata stays repo-wide
  (fail-safe: stale guidance beats none).
- Same-run multi-file sweeps: a frontmatter-less THREAT_MODEL.md gets
  the same default concept id for every file, so under
  UNIQUE(run_id, concept_id) scanning file 2 evicted file 1's threat
  model row on INSERT OR REPLACE. File-scoped concepts now qualify
  their id with the resource; widening the unique index instead would
  require a schema version bump that forces users to delete their
  databases.

Change-Id: I30c46d5ecaa057f924a14f20390b0f08f6a78e01
